facts.value: Citizen journalism is reporting by people who are not professional journalists. They can be ordinary citizens who write or conduct research using the internet, blogs, social media, or even provide instant text or video reporting from the scene.

Citizen journalism can be useful when reporting incidents that even local newspapers and broadcast stations are not able to reach, such as a disaster in a remote area or political upheaval in countries where print and broadcast media are controlled by the government.
In addition to traditional forms, journalism continues to expand into specialized fields shaped by technology and societal needs.
